keenable.snippet:
The Trump administration has officially backed Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia—a little over a week after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the AI giant needed a “dramatic shake-up” of leadership.
Huang and Nvidia, the company he founded in 1993, are currently subject to [intense scrutiny](https://fortune.com/2026/11/09/jensen-huangs-net-worth-ai-rout-drop-affair-admit/) after it emerged that Huang had conducted an extramarital affair with a woman believed to be a Chinese spy. The company and its leadership are now facing questions from Congress and U.S. law enforcement about their compliance with export controls on specialized chips to China.

President Trump [wrote on Truth Social ](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/117663497310955803)this morning: “I hope the board of Nvidia rehires Jensen Huang. It would be the best thing for the company, and also, for the U.S.A.”
The president has been lenient on Huang, despite Congressional concerns that Huang’s relationship with an alleged Chinese asset was a national security risk. [Nvidia has said](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/statement-from-nvidia-board-of-directors) it does not believe U.S. or company secrets have been compromised. Despite that, Trump [said he is a “brilliant person”](https://www.facebook.com/ABCNews/videos/president-trump-on-former-nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang/2218145089080933/) who made some “bad decisions.”
